items.problem: Migrated app's orientation output is dead: NativeOrientation/CurrentOrientation show 'N/A' and AutoRotationPreferences shows a raw exception, because DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView() throws on WinUI 3 desktop and the agent had no working replacement.
items.evidence: migration-score.json feature 'Show and lock orientation' verdict=partial; discrepancies.md HIGH: 'DisplayInformation not available on desktop... GetForCurrentView must be called on a thread associated with a CoreWindow'; build-events shows agent shipped try/catch printing ex.Message.
items.skill_search: grepped MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md for DisplayInformation / GetForCurrentView / orientation
items.wrong_text_if_any: | `DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView()` | `XamlRoot.RasterizationScale` or Win32 `GetDpiForWindow` |  (also the section preamble 'None of the GetForCurrentView() patterns work in WinUI 3 desktop')
items.root_cause: The #getforcurrentview mapping presents DPI as the ONLY replacement for DisplayInformation and the section blanket-claims none of these APIs 'work', so the agent concluded display orientation has no desktop equivalent and degraded to a broken fallback. In fact the Windows App SDK ships Microsoft.Graphics.Display.DisplayInformation with a CreateForWindowId(windowId) factory that preserves every member (orientation, DPI, color info).
items.proposed_fix: In MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #getforcurrentview: (1) soften the preamble from 'None ... work' to 'the GetForCurrentView() *entry point* is gone — replace each with a window-scoped factory or AppWindow'; (2) change the DisplayInformation row to point at `DisplayInformation.CreateForWindowId(windowId)` (Microsoft.Graphics.Display) with RasterizationScale/GetDpiForWindow noted as the DPI-only shortcut; (3) add a short code snippet showing windowId acquisition and CurrentOrientation.
items.generalizes: Any UWP app that reads display metrics or orientation (DisplayInformation is the standard UWP path for DPI, orientation, and HDR/color info) hits GetForCurrentView() on desktop. A correct one-line mapping + snippet fixes the whole family, not just this sample.
